title: The Iterative Dynamical System Generated by 2x-1
content: The increasing map F(x)=2^x-1 on [0,1] determines a two-sided orbit of weights at each interior point. We establish an exact greedy normalization of these weights and study its boundary and carry thresholds. The two normalized endpoint linearizations define a single positive periodic connection function. We show that this function determines convergent expansions of every order for both threshold sequences and can itself be recovered from the boundary sequence. A self-contained interval certificate proves that its first Fourier coefficient is nonzero and that there is exactly one maximum and one minimum per period. The normalized boundary roots consequently fail to converge, although their oscillation has width only about 2.51342 × 10⁻²⁵. The same certificate shows that every C¹ diffeomorphism of the closed interval commuting with F is an integer iterate. Let P be the attracting coordinate, normalized by P(0)=0, P′(0)=1, and P(F(x))=(ln 2)P(x). Continuing P along the negative real axis, we prove that its local inverse has a unique nearest logarithmic singularity at -R, where R=-P(-1)/ln 2. Its Taylor coefficient of degree n has an explicit exponentially smaller correction involving 1/ln n. The analytic reductions and singularity theorems are proved in full. The least-period and shape conclusions use a reproducible finite interval calculation, together with explicit analytic bounds for all infinite tails.
